title: The node wrapper orphans the native quest child when the wrapper is killed (DEC-282 (a1) item 7)
description:
CARRIER from ODOC-610 / DEC-282 (a1) ADDED 2026-11-19, opum-doc, after the clock read 02:29:29Z on cont1's follow-up over opum-comm. Read BY REF from opum-doc origin/dev 68734a01 (.quest/planning.json, decision DEC-282, outcome (a1)).

Verbatim from (a1), item 7: "The node wrapper must never orphan the native child. It forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to the child, and exits with the child's status. On the wrapper's own death the child must not outlive it: run it in its own process group and kill the group, or use an equivalent that leaves no orphan. Proof: a test that kills the wrapper mid-run and finds no surviving quest process. The same rule applies to lore's wrapper if it has one; lore-cli checks."

The live case, also verbatim: "A live case on mbam5 at 02:24Z: the Mac's load was 41, with 4-9 concurrent `quest task list --across-refs --allow-partial --json` processes each running 60-90 s, many orphaned (PPID 1). The caller, a status daemon polling on a 500 ms watch and a 5 s tick with a 60 s timeout, killed only the node wrapper (quest.cjs), so the native quest binary kept running. The repository has 2,313 tasks and 47 worktrees of one clone."

Item 7 is the most urgent of (a1), "because an orphaned native process is a resource leak for any caller with a timeout." It ships with DEC-282 items 1-5 and 8 in the next lore/quest pair release.

Target: bin/quest.cjs (the node wrapper that spawns the native binary) and its tests.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Killing the node wrapper mid-run leaves no surviving quest process: it runs the native child in its own process group and kills the group on its own death, or uses an equivalent that leaves no orphan
The wrapper forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to the native child and exits with the child's status
A regression test kills the wrapper mid-run and asserts no quest process survives, and that test goes red when the forwarding and group-kill are removed (both directions proven)
bun run check exits 0 with the new test included

implementationNotes: HELD 2026-11-19T03:46:17Z on the leader ruling: bin/quest.cjs is DEC-182 (1) launcher class, the same ruling given for lore bin/lore.cjs, on the rule that when unsure it is sensitive. It is built by a sonnet-or-higher quest-cli session with an opus security review and no DeepSeek at any step; a deepseek-flash session (this one) must not touch bin/quest.cjs. Evidence that it is the launcher in this repository own vocabulary: package.json bin.quest is ./bin/quest.cjs; scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs refuses unless "Root package must be a Node launcher" and pins the packed file set to LICENSE, README.md, bin/quest.cjs, package.json; test/qcli399-launcher-equivalence.test.ts compares "the qualified X-rc.N launcher and the published X launcher" on that same file.

Hold removed 2026-11-18 on the leader brief: this quest-cli session is the successor renewed onto claude-sonnet-5-5, the sonnet-or-higher tier DEC-282 (a1) item 7 requires for launcher-class bin/quest.cjs (DEC-182 (1)). Opus security review follows; no DeepSeek at any step.

Built: bin/quest.cjs now uses async spawn; forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the child; exits with the child status (128+signo when the child dies by a signal); off a TTY the child runs in its own process group (kill/sweep of the group, including on wrapper exit); on a TTY it stays in the foreground group to avoid SIGTTIN. Proof: test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts (stand-in native script with a grandchild sleep). Red with the original spawnSync wrapper (4 fail) and red with the forwarding handlers removed (3 fail); green with the fix (5 pass), 3 consecutive runs. Known limit, documented in the wrapper: SIGKILL of the wrapper cannot be intercepted. AC4 (bun run check) left unchecked: local bun 1.3.14 lags the repo pin; CI is the evidence. No dependency, CI, release-path or package-file-set change.

Round-1 security review of #744 at 1099a777: REQUEST_CHANGES. AC1 unchecked (B2): SIGKILL of the wrapper still orphans the child, so it is met only for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP and uncaught-exception exits; the signal the live mbam5 caller timeout sends is UNDETERMINED (Node/Bun spawn timeouts default to SIGTERM, fixed here; Go CommandContext and Rust Child::kill send SIGKILL, not fixed). Must be established before this closes. B1 PENDING A DESIGN RULING (via opum-doc, with lore #734 which placed the group the other way): off a TTY detached:true calls setsid, so a caller group SIGKILL (kill -9 -pgid, killpg) now reaches only the wrapper and orphans the child, which the old spawnSync wrapper never did; staying in the caller group would keep that working but cannot sweep grandchildren. N3 (exit 128+n vs re-raising the child signal on the wrapper) likewise held. PREDICTIONS for the round-2 mutants, written before any run: (M1) detached:false with forwarding kept: the three signal tests go red at the no-survivor assertion (grandchild sleep survives); status-mapping, stdin and spawn-failure tests stay green. (M2) original spawnSync wrapper: three signal tests red at no-survivor, status-mapping red, spawn-failure green (control). (M3) status guard removed: spawn-failure test red (exit 243), all others green. (M4) forwarding handlers removed: three signal tests red. (M5) isatty swapped back to process.stdin.isTTY: stdin-pipe test MAY go red; no prediction, will report measured.

Round 2 applied (a1 comment corrected with the trade-off; isatty(0) replaces process.stdin.isTTY; handlers registered before spawn; spawn failure exits 1; test ordering/cleanup/skipIf/dead ternary; new stdin-pipe and spawn-failure tests). Mutants vs the predictions above: M1 detached:false: 3 signal tests red, rest green - as predicted. M2 original spawnSync: 3 signal tests + status-mapping red, spawn-failure green - as predicted. M3 guard removed: spawn-failure test red only - as predicted. M4 handlers removed: 3 signal tests red - as predicted. M5 stdin.isTTY: NO test went red (7 pass) - the stdin-pipe test does not detect the O_NONBLOCK concern with a cat stand-in, so it pins intact delivery, not that the getter is harmless; isatty(0) is taken on reasoning, not on a demonstrated failure. B1 and N3 remain held for the design ruling.

DEC-282 (a2) applied in round 3 (design: keep the own-group shape; re-raise the child signal; TERM-then-KILL documented; lifeline = separate carrier). PREDICTIONS written before the round-3 mutants: (M6) re-raise replaced by exitCode=128+n with no self-kill: ONLY the signal-death test goes red. (M7) ownGroup forced false: the off-TTY group test and the 3 signal-sweep tests go red; the on-TTY test stays green. (M8) ownGroup forced true: ONLY the on-TTY foreground-group test goes red. (M9) the sweepGroup() call before the re-raise removed: no firm prediction; the SIGINT signal test (grandchild sleep ignores SIGINT) is the candidate, others stay green.

Round-3 mutants vs predictions: M6 (no re-raise) only the signal-death test red - as predicted. M7 (ownGroup false) off-TTY group test + 3 sweep tests red, on-TTY green - as predicted. M8 (ownGroup true) only the on-TTY test red - as predicted. M9 (sweep before re-raise removed): 0 red - NO test covered it; added a test (child dies by SIGTERM leaving a grandchild; wrapper must sweep before re-raising) which goes red under M9 and is green with the fix. Tests: 10 pass. On-TTY proof uses script(1) with /dev/null stdin (a bun "pipe" is a socket script rejects); skipped if script is absent. CHANGELOG Unreleased entry states the SIGKILL/group-SIGKILL residual and the TERM-then-KILL remedy. The lifeline (item 2) is NOT in this PR; its carrier task follows.

DEC-282 (a4): AC1 (killing the wrapper leaves no surviving quest process) waits on QCLI-571 under (a4), because a lore-spawned wrapper has piped stdout and stderr and so owns a separate group that a group SIGKILL of lore does not reach. QCLI-571 does not block the pair release; it is the first item of the patch release after it. AC1 stays unchecked until QCLI-571 lands.
